summary: Submitted a focused follow-up experiment for the open question the last interpretation recorded: whether the 'leadership transfer in progress' error returned to an explicit transfer to a demoted member belongs to that request or to a transfer already running when it arrived. The harness demotes a follower, waits until that member's own configuration view reports the non-voter role, then in one case issues exactly one explicit transfer while sampling the leader's transfer flag before the call, right after the future is returned, after the future completes and after a settle; in the second case it reproduces the five-attempt sequence and samples the flag before every attempt, recording each attempt's error. Both cases sample leadership every ten milliseconds for three seconds and record whether the named member ever led. Local verification shows the flag clear in every sample, a single attempt completing with no error, and the named member never leading, which is enough to say the target is not installed; the run also indicates the in-progress outcome depends on the earlier harness's own sequencing, which this request will settle on a recorded receipt. The request declares both case events as prerequisites with role and convergence conditions, asserts target_became_leader on the single case and flag_before_first == false on the retry case, reuses only registered transfer sources, states no requirement and carries no anchors, and validates against submission.schema.json.
